read_extent.submission: Official cover and contents; complete summary physical pages 6–8; complete relevant support subsection 3.1 physical pages 11–16 and adjacent direct-marketing context 17–19. Not claiming a full read of all 58 physical pages.
read_extent.primary_study: All 15 study pages, including original summary, scenario assumptions, detailed prices and value components, household illustration, modelling limitations and methodology. Physical pages 7–8 and author physical 15 visually checked.
read_extent.exact_draft: BT 21/7867,7 September 2026: cover and overview plus physical pages 22–24 and 30, containing operative support and transition provisions. No later version substituted.

issues.assessment: The detailed study means 112.8 without versus 89.3 with solar, yielding approximately 26.32% higher without, while 20.83% is the reduction from the higher baseline. Rounding 20.8 to 20 cannot repair that denominator reversal. However, the primary study's own summary says approximately 21% higher without; the submission follows that flawed summary formulation. Preserve this prominently, and do not frame the author as independently inventing or contradicting an otherwise consistent source.
issues.materiality: Minor because this is auxiliary, the absolute price difference and beneficial direction remain, and the correction strengthens the pro-solar rationale. False direction is appropriate independently of severity.
issues.limits: The modelled no-solar counterfactual is not observed fact. No corrected prediction for a particular household, no full cost-benefit conclusion, and no inference of intent.

issues.assessment: The source explicitly partitions 13.1 billion wholesale-price value and 2.6 billion export receipts. Its 15.7 combined value is valid within its model, but the author's explicit lower-consumer-cost description changes the category. The surrounding paragraph primarily discusses price reductions and household/industry cost savings. Its final broad national-economy statement makes aggregate-benefit shorthand a substantial benign reading, which limits the allegation but does not make export receipts themselves a consumer price reduction.
issues.materiality: Minor and favourable to the request because adding export receipts enlarges the stated consumer-cost component. Do not call the combined 44%or roughly 40% comparison mathematically false; it matches the combined figure. The 13.1 figure is only the study's modelled price component, not actual realised consumer savings.
issues.limits: Export receipts can have legitimate wider benefits and indirect effects on consumers. The record does not establish those effects zero, that support is uneconomic, or that every customer receives the modelled price benefit.

distinctness: These can be separate issues: one reverses the percentage-comparison denominator; the other relabels a valid aggregate's components. They have different corrections and opposite directions. Neither should be split further into duplicate 40%or household-benefit records.
quotation_note: No additional original quotations or invented author response. Existing short source fragments and shared request are sufficient.
